newsitem.title: USA: Las Vegas casino king has art world taking notice.
newsitem.headline: Las Vegas casino king has art world taking notice.

text.p: Las Vegas casino king Stephen Wynn has entered the high-stakes art auction world, buying his second multi-million-dollar painting in two days.
Wynn peeled $3.4 million from his bankroll on Wednesday night at Christie's auction to buy Pablo Picasso's "Gosol," a 1906 painting of a Spanish village done at the end of the artist's rose period.

It was his second major purchase in two days. On Tuesday night at Sotheby's, Wynn paid $2.9 million for a Manet drawing that will be on display at Bellagio, his latest casino being built in Las Vegas.
There was no immediate word on his plans for the Picasso.
Among buyers of the top ten paintings at the sale, Wynn was the only one willing to let his name be known.

Two people who asked to remain anonymous paid the top prices of the night -- $13.2 million each for two Claude Monet paintings -- one a view of the artist's garden at Vetheuil and the other a painting of water lillies called "Nympheas," painted at the end of his life when his eyesight was failing.
The sale of impressionist and modern works at Christie's fetched about $82.9 million, with pre-sale estimates ranging between $70 million and $92 million.
Christie's New York chairman Christopher Burgge said that 80 percent of the lots on offer were sold.
The third highest price in the sale was $7.2 million paid for a Degas study of a nude leaving the bath.
